scripts.//schemas: @finance/schemas is consumed as compiled output, so it is built before anything that reads its types. `npm ci` also builds it through the package's own `prepare` script.
scripts.dev: npm run build:schemas && npm run dev --workspace=@finance/api
scripts.build: npm run build:schemas && npm run build --workspace=@finance/api
scripts.test: npm run build:schemas && npm run test --workspace=@finance/api
scripts.test:unit: npm run build:schemas && npm run test:unit --workspace=@finance/api
scripts.typecheck: npm run build:schemas && npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present
scripts.generate:openapi: npm run build:schemas && npm run generate:openapi --workspace=@finance/api && npm run generate:types --workspace=@finance/web
scripts.check:openapi: npm run build:schemas && npm run check:openapi --workspace=@finance/api && npm run check:types --workspace=@finance/web
scripts.infra:up: docker compose up -d postgres redis mailhog
scripts.infra:reset: docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d postgres redis mailhog
scripts.//openapi: The contract chain: the API generates docs/openapi.json from the router, and the client generates its response types from that file. Both steps run together so the two can never be regenerated apart.
